paragraphs: Friend, here's what hits me about this passage. Jesus knows ALL that is coming upon Him (John 18:4), and He doesn't run, He doesn't hide, He steps forward. Nobody drags Him into that garden. He walks toward the cup the Father has given Him (John 18:11). So when this story gets heavy, and it's about to, remember that Jesus is not a man things happen to. He is choosing love with His eyes wide open.

Now look at what He does while the soldiers stand there with their torches. He's the one about to be arrested, and He's still looking out for His own: "let these men go" (John 18:8). The writer says this fulfills the word He had spoken: "I have not lost one of those You have given Me." (John 18:9). I think that should settle something in your heart. If you belong to Jesus, He is holding on to you, even when the night is dark and the crowd is loud.

Then there's Peter, swinging a sword and cutting off Malchus's ear (John 18:10). I know that feeling, friend. I've grabbed the sword when I should've trusted the plan, and my sword was usually a rolling pin. Jesus says, "Put your sword back in its sheath!" (John 18:11), because the Father's way is bigger than our panic. This story isn't over, and neither is the teaching, so stay with me.
